3_description:
new from-scratch round-3 family `models_r3/r3s1_twostage_crosscoef`; condition-only forward signature; stripped view only; leakage tripwire; no LF array opened at any stage; **no gradient-trained arm** (every arm closed-form).
- **Scored column `test_hf`** — two-stage propagation-aware cross-coefficient head. Stage 1 is the shipped head unchanged (centering `ratio = ||mean_i y_i|| / geomean_i ||y_i||`, tau = 1.0 over {fact, add}; bank = {DC/spatial-mean} u {POD 0-49 of the DC-removed fit-fold residual in the selected centering form}; per direction a 5-fold OOF R^2 from the condition over {affine, quadratic, RBF kernel ridge, k-NN}, best family out of fold; SET = directions clearing tau = 0.1, min 1, max 32). **Stage 2 (new)**: remaining directions regressed on the **out-of-fold stage-1 predicted** SET coefficients over the same map bank, with the stage-2 gate both **selected and fitted** on those OOF predictions (tau2 = 0.1). Empty gate => bitwise no-op.
- **Reference arms**: `ref_head_onestage` (the shipped law; matched folds/bases/seed — paired control *and* reproduction seam), `ref_twostage_true_gate` (F25 negative control, reported as a named rediscovery), `ref_dc_only` (the condition->level law, required by round-3 success criterion 1), floors `ref_zero` / `ref_train_mean` / `ref_nn_condition` (seam-checked to `state/anchors_repaired/floors.json` at 1e-9, RAISING on mismatch), `ref_affine_on_hf_train` (seam-checked on both ifc cells to `launch_anchors.json:ifc_floors_repaired`, reported on the sharp cells).
- **Diagnostic columns (L3-bearing)**: per direction and per cell, OOF R^2 (A) from the condition vs (B) from the SET coefficients, the margin B - A, the stage-2 gate size, and the per-cell 3-seed spread of every scored quantity (handed to `r3s4_audit` for mce re-certification). Instrument: `round2/tools/coefficient_factorisation_audit.py`, adapted on use.
- **Folds**: identical to the shipped head so the control is procedure-matched — disjoint 80/10/10, 5 resamples, LOO when `N_train < 20`; the calibration fold is **asserted unused** (no post-hoc stage in this card) rather than merged, keeping the fit fold at exactly 320 rows so the reproduction seam is meaningful.
- **Build gates**: **G-A** reproduction seam (`ref_head_onestage` per-cell 3-seed mean within 3 % of `launch_anchors.json:cards.r2s1_direct-B3.per_dataset_mean_skill`, panel geomean within 28.2174 +/- 0.3612; RAISE, INFRA-class); **G-B** floor seam checks at 1e-9; **G-C** stripped-view leakage tripwire + guard set at the same tier; **G-D** target-scaler pre-flight (`tools/target_scale_spread_audit.py`) on pfc and cahn_hilliard before any test tensor is touched; **G-E** stage-2 no-op assertion (empty gate => `test_hf` == `ref_head_onestage` to 1e-12, which bounds the panel delta below by 0).

interpretation: [FACT] The card's cond_dim discriminator is wrong and the correct variable is stage-1 residual saturation. Stage 2 can act only where stage 1 left in-bank energy behind AND that leftover is predictable from stage-1's predicted coefficients. On the 5-cell scored panel exactly one cell satisfies both. The pre-registered 4-high vs 2-low cond_dim split has no support; the operative split is 1-vs-4 on E_rem x reachability.

[HYPOTHESIS M1, moderate confidence] The stage-2 gate is a CONDITIONING/REPRESENTATION effect, not new information. Its input f(condition) is a deterministic function of the condition, so g(f(condition)) cannot contain information the condition lacks - yet pod_5 moves from OOF R^2 -0.0059 (best of {affine, quadratic, RBF-KR, kNN} on a 19-d condition, 320 rows) to 0.6696 (the same four families on a 3-d input). The economical reading is that the 3-direction SET is a learned low-dimensional coordinate of the coarsening state in which the downstream regression is well-posed and in 19-d is not. FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION: any comparable 19-d -> 3-d reduction (PCA of the condition, a random 3-d projection refit, the true-SET coordinates) should reproduce most of the effect. Not tested here.

[HYPOTHESIS M2, high confidence - CONFIRMED in turn 3B] The propagation-aware input is a net LOSS wherever the SET is capped. On fisher_kpp the stage-2 input destroys 0.0713 of encoded energy worth of condition-reachable signal (r2_cond ~0.30 -> r2_set ~0), and the residual-energy attribution puts 17x more of affine's advantage outside the SET than inside it. The corollary lever is not a better stage 2 but raising SELECT_MAX above 32, or feeding stage 2 [predicted SET coefficients, condition] instead of predicted coefficients alone.

[HYPOTHESIS M4, moderate-high confidence] The F25 reversal is a train/test input-distribution mismatch, exactly as the 'propagation-aware' framing predicted. stage2.py:124-190: ref_twostage_true_gate selects and fits its gate on the TRUE stage-1 coefficients but predict_coefficients is 'ALWAYS fed the stage-1 head's PREDICTED coefficients', while the scored arm fits and predicts on the same (OOF-predicted) distribution. Turn 1 measured the gap on pod_5: OOF R^2 0.9410 from true coefficients vs 0.6696 from predicted. At +0.366 vs tau_rel 0.36125 = 1.01x this is DIRECTIONALLY CONFIRMED, MAGNITUDE UNRESOLVED, and it is a rediscovery of Spyromitros-Xioufis et al. (arXiv:1211.6581), not a finding.

[HYPOTHESIS M6, high confidence - supersedes turn 2's M3] cahn_hilliard is a NON-IDENTIFIABILITY split, not an extrapolation split. The 27 hard rows are statistically indistinguishable from the easy rows in condition space (max 0.448 sigma, NN-distance ratio 1.018) while their fields are 3.3x farther from anything in training. Two samples with nearly the same 19-d IC-coefficient vector produce very different late-time coarsening morphologies: the condition vector is INCOMPLETE for this cell on a fixed ~27% subpopulation. No condition-only architecture - this head, a larger head, or a trained network - can repair that, so the cell's achievable skill is capped by the hard-row mixture weight. The oracle nearest-train-field score of 0.4202 on those rows (vs the head's 1.0632) shows the fields themselves are not unpredictable, only unpredictable FROM THIS CONDITION.

[FACT] The three 'unpredicted negatives' are two mechanisms plus one non-event. (i) fisher_kpp's losses to both ref_dc_only and ref_affine_on_hf_train are one mechanism - a stage-1 capacity cap, upstream of everything this card built and untouched by stage 2. (ii) The F25 reversal is a distinct stage-2 input-distribution mechanism. (iii) allen_cahn's and ifc_heat's affine 'losses' are below their own certified floors and should be struck from the negatives list. What (i) and (ii) share is that both are stage-1-quality-limited: where the condition->coefficient law is capped or imprecise, the two-stage construction inherits the deficit.

7_gap_and_future.open_question: The stage-2 gate's input f(condition) is a deterministic function of the condition, so g(f(condition)) can carry no information the condition lacks - yet on cahn_hilliard's pod_5 the OOF R^2 moves from -0.0059 (best of {affine, quadratic, RBF-KR, kNN} on the 19-d condition, 320 rows) to 0.6696 (the same four families on the 3-d predicted SET coefficients). The answer decides whether 'propagation-aware two-stage' is a real architectural principle or a lucky dimensionality reduction, and it is cheap and closed-form to settle: swap stage 2's input for (a) PCA-3 of the condition, (b) a random 3-d projection of the condition, (c) the TRUE SET coefficients under a matched fit/predict distribution, and (d) [predicted SET coefficients, condition] concatenated. If (a) and (b) recover most of the 0.67, the mechanism is conditioning and the two-stage framing should be retired in favour of a stated reduction step; if only (c)/(d) do, the propagation structure is doing real work.
